qs.q: An infant presents with macrocephaly and symptoms of increased intracranial pressure. Neuroimaging reveals an intraventricular papillary neoplasm in the lateral ventricles. Which tumor is most likely?
qs.e: Choroid plexus tumors are the most frequent CNS tumor in infants under 1 year of age, occurring predominantly supratentorially in the lateral ventricles. They typically present with signs of increased intracranial pressure and macrocephaly in infants.

qs.q: In an infant whose cranial sutures have not yet fused, increased intracranial pressure most commonly leads to:
qs.e: Open sutures allow the skull to expand, producing a large head (macrocephaly). Adults with closed sutures would instead develop raised ICP without head enlargement.

qs.q: Which pathological entity is classified as a compensatory ventricular enlargement due to a loss of brain parenchyma rather than true increased intracranial pressure?
qs.e: Hydrocephalus ex vacuo occurs due to neurodegeneration or infarcts resulting in loss of brain parenchyma, and it does not raise intracranial pressure. True hydrocephalus involves excessive CSF accumulation that typically elevates intracranial pressure.
